name: Deadeye Shore
summary: Along Durotar’s eastern edge, Deadeye Shore stretches east of Drygulch Ravine. Its barren sands take their name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the Bleeding Hollow chieftain, while raptors, scorpids, and feral boars roam the coast.

sections.title: A Shoreline of the Bleeding Hollow
sections.body:
Beneath central Durotar’s red bluffs, Deadeye Shore runs past sand and rocky outcrops shaped faintly like a skull with one empty eye socket. The coast is named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed Bleeding Hollow chieftain who fought in the First and Second Wars.

No great settlement or military outpost holds this shore. Aggressive beasts roam the sands, and Burning Blade cultists from nearby ravine hideouts have been seen prowling toward the water.

faq.q: Why is it called Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: Kilrogg Deadeye, the famed Bleeding Hollow chieftain, gave the shore its name. Its rocky outcrops also faintly resemble a skull with one empty eye socket.
No permanent settlements occupy Deadeye Shore. Raptors, scorpids, and boars roam the coast, while fishermen and travelers sometimes pass through and may meet hidden Burning Blade cultists.

faq.q: What threats are found around Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: Aggressive beasts roam Deadeye Shore, and Burning Blade cultists from neighboring Drygulch Ravine sometimes descend from its rocky canyons. They ambush unwary travelers and fishermen.

angles.text: As an orc, you see a shore named for Kilrogg Deadeye. It recalls the old chieftains who shaped the Horde’s history during the wars on Azeroth.
